title: Japan Ke 3 Paise Wale Tarike
note:
METHOD ONE — MOTTAINAI. The video's hinge lands on this chapter's first
     frame (the s33->s34 shove lives on the concat boundary, not inside here),
     so everything before was why the story is wrong and everything from here is
     what to do anyway.

     Ground arc: neutral warm on the word itself -> cool on "regret, not
     instruction" -> warm through the chain that made one shirt -> red on the
     hours it cost -> GREEN HELD ACROSS THE THREE CHECKS, deepening once per
     check -> red on what the checks found -> cool on the question -> green on
     the question itself -> neutral for the arithmetic -> warm out.

     Archetypes: A A D A B B B A A D B A A. B is HELD across s38/s39/s40 —
     three checks are one instruction, so the layout stays put and the measure
     bar under it moves a third at a time. That bar is the only thing in the
     chapter that carries ACROSS scenes, and it is what breaks the uniform
     +0.30/+1.10/+1.90 ladder the ch2 review asked to break at least once.

     Ten of thirteen scenes are art-off. The photographs here are unusually
     literal — kintsugi, a mended hem, a cotton field, a loom, a truck, tagged
     clothes, a fridge shelf, unopened boxes — and every drawn layer proposed
     over them was a redrawing of the same object. What survived asserts what a
     photograph cannot: a decision rule (s43) and a count (s44).

s34.comment:
4.1 · A · PLATE · no role · neutral warm — MOTTAINAI. Kintsugi: the repair is
     worth more than the break. The word is the subject; nothing is drawn on it.

s35.comment:
4.2 · A · PLATE · no role · cool — NOT A SCOLDING. The coolest frame in the
     chapter's opening, because "regret, not instruction" is the correction.

s36.comment:
4.3 · D · BAND · no role · warm — ONE SHIRT. Three declared framings and
     three real photographs: the cotton field, the loom, the truck. The chain IS
     the picture, three times over, so a drawn chain on top of it would only
     trace what is already there.

s37.comment:
4.4 · A · PLATE · warn · red — AND YOURS. A measure bar of "hours you worked
     for it" was drawn and cut: the script names no number, and a bar a viewer
     can read off is a statistic whether or not one was meant (the lesson
     ch2's household grid cost).

s38.comment:
4.5 · B · FIGURE · fund · green — CHECK ONE. The three checks are one
     instruction, so B is held for all three and the bar under the type moves a
     third per scene. It is the only element in the cut that continues across a
     cut, and it is what makes three separate scenes read as one list.

s39.comment:
4.6 · B · FIGURE · fund · green deeper — CHECK TWO. The bar picks up at
     exactly where check one left it.

s40.comment: 4.7 · B · FIGURE · fund · green deepest — CHECK THREE. The bar closes.

s41.comment:
4.8 · A · PLATE · warn · red hot — WHAT YOU SAW. Unopened boxes. The chapter
     turns here and the ground is its hottest.

s42.comment:
4.9 · A · PLATE · no role · cool — IT IS ONE QUESTION. An empty shelf with one
     object; the frame goes quiet before the rule lands.

s43.comment:
4.10 · D · BAND · fund · green — THE QUESTION, and the chapter's one piece of
     real drawn argument. One path in, two out, and the MAYBE branch struck
     through: that is the rule the line states, and no photograph of an object on
     a table can state a decision rule. The strike is hand-weighted and
     round-capped, the same hand as ch2's tick.

s44.comment:
4.11 · B · FIGURE · no role · neutral — ON ₹30,000. "Three or four times a
     month" is a COUNT, which is the one thing a photograph of a shopping bag
     cannot hold. Four tally strokes; the fourth arrives faint, because the line
     says three OR four and a solid fourth would overstate it.

4.12 · A · PLATE · no role · neutral warm — THE WHOLE POINT. A worn sandal
     beside a new one still in its box; the photograph is the argument entire.
